scripts.title: GridDraw Animation: 1-bit font and sprite editor/animator
scripts.description: The owner's BitFontMaker2-compatible editor (10/27/2026): draws 1-bit characters and 16x16/32x32 video game sprites on a grid of any size, stores them as binary strings and PBM images (not graphic objects), animates actors with frames, loops and ping-pong, undo/redo, Aquarius font export, PNG export. Mostly globals so values can be checked in the Message Box. Source of LIB_BIT's pure grid handlers.

scripts.title: Bitmap Vector Tracer: draw 1-bit, trace to vector graphics
scripts.description: The owner's tracer stack (11/09/2026): draw with the mouse into a 1-bit grid held as a string of 1s and 0s shown as a PBM image, then turn it into LiveCode graphics: per-bit rectangles, merged runs, outlines (doTrace / radialSweep), digitize sequences, deresolution, play the drawing history back, BitFontMaker2 mass import. scripts.title: Vibecode3D engine: vector 3D engine and editor in pure LiveCode
scripts.description: The owner's 3D engine (~8000 lines): 1983 Star Wars arcade / Vectrex wireframes drawn with LiveCode line graphics. Fixed 33 ms loop (game.loop.*), a fast renderer folding camera and object rotation into one 3x3 matrix (Mat3.*, Xform.Object, RenderMeshInto with depth bands), procedural meshes (Mesh.*, MeshBox/Prism/Lathe/Loft/Grid), entities and colour batching, movement, collisions, particles, derez FX, lasers, a vector font HUD, view presets, audio, menus from templates, game cards (Play.<game>) with rebuild, picking without triangles. World axes: +X right, +Y DOWN, +Z forward.

scripts.title: LIB_BIT: pure 1-bit grid handlers (Bit.*)
scripts.description: Grids as text (one line per row, "1" filled): blank, size, count, invert, shift, flip, rotate, pad, to and from PBM, to and from row numbers and long strings. Every handler is pure: no globals, fields or images. Made from GridDraw and the tracer.
header: LIB_BIT: 1-bit grids for sprites, fonts and maps.
A grid is text: one line per row, one character per pixel, "1" filled, "0" empty.
Any width and height. Every handler here is pure: it takes grids and returns grids,
touching no globals, fields or images, so it works the same in a stack, a
standalone or a server.
start using stack "<path>/LIB_BIT/livecode/lib_bit.livecodescript"

scripts.title: LIB_TRACE: bitmap to outline polygons (Trace.*)
scripts.description: Pure outline tracing: an image mask or 1-bit grid to contour polygons (Trace.Contours), then offset and scale the points for graphics or meshes. Made from the Bitmap Vector Tracer.
header: LIB_TRACE: bitmap -> shapes. Outline tracing: bitmap to polygon points.
(Grid to 3D map moved to LIB_MAP: Map.Pieces.)
Pure handlers: data in, data out; no globals, custom properties, graphics or screen.
start using stack "<path>/LIB_TRACE/livecode/lib_trace.livecodescript"
put Trace.MaskToGrid(the maskData of image "logo", the width of image "logo", \
the height of image "logo") into tGrid

scripts.title: LIB_MAP: game levels from 1-bit grids (Map.*)
scripts.description: Stitch grid sections into a world, check seams, list floors and walls, pathfinding for AI, merge open space into navigation regions, block edges and meshes for 3D (Map.Blocks, Map.BlockEdges). Pure; used by xt3d and Vibecode3D (the Face card).
header: LIB_MAP: levels from 1-bit grids. Stitch sections into a world, check the seams,
list floors and walls, find paths for AI, merge open space into navigation regions,
and build mesh data for 3D. Pure handlers: data in, data out. For xt3d and Vibecode3D.
start using stack "<path>/LIB_MAP/livecode/lib_map.livecodescript"
GRIDS are LIB_BIT's format, one line per row:  "1" = wall,  "0" = open floor.
(A sprite drawn the other way round: Bit.Invert.) Cells are "col,row", 1-based,

scripts.title: LIB_MCP: a local HTTP dev server inside LiveCode (DevServer.*)
scripts.description: Lets Claude Code, a local model or any local tool drive a running LiveCode IDE or standalone: run code, evaluate, compile-check a script, read translated errors, snapshot a stack, reload it. Plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a token file; sockets, accept connections, error translation, pending-message handling.
header: LIB_MCP: lets Claude Code, a local model (through MCP) or any local tool drive a running
LiveCode 9.6.3 IDE or standalone: run code, evaluate, compile-check, read errors, snapshot.
https: none. Plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only. A script-only library stack.
START IT
* from any stack:  start using stack "<path>/LIB_MCP/livecode/lib_mcp.livecodescript"
DevServer.Start 8766, "<name of the stack /run should talk to>"

scripts.title: LIB_DEVSERVER: the dev server as a Vibecode3D LIB_ card (origin of LIB_MCP)
scripts.description: The first version of LIB_MCP, written as a LIB_ card loaded with Lib.Load. Kept to show the card-library pattern and how the server grew.
header: LIB_DEVSERVER  -  lets Claude Code (or any local tool) talk to the running IDE.
Loaded like every LIB_ card: Lib.Load "DEVSERVER", then DevServer.Start.
APP.init starts it automatically in the IDE (never in a standalone).
Plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only, every request must carry the header
X-Token: <token>
The token is new on every start and is written, with the port, to the file

scripts.title: LIB_XTJSON: rebuild stacks from an XTJSON harvest
scripts.description: Reads XTJSON/manifest.json and the stack_*.json files from an LCHarvest2 export and builds the stacks again: cards, groups, controls, properties, custom property sets, scripts, images. JSON parsing in pure LiveCode.
scripts.notes: An older copy (669 lines) is in Vibecode3D/LIB_XTJSON.livecodescript.
header: LIB_XTJSON -- rebuild LiveCode stacks from an LCHarvest2 export
Target: LiveCode 9.6.3.
WHAT IT DOES
Reads XTJSON/manifest.json and every stack_*.json, then builds new stacks
in memory: cards, controls (groups nested), properties, custom properties,
images, behaviors and scripts. Nothing is saved to disk except the report.

scripts.title: xt_error_capture: copy the text out of the IDE error window
scripts.description: Reads the field inside LiveCode 9.6.3's revErrorDisplay palette so error text can be saved instead of retyped. Untested when written.
header: xt_error_capture -- copy the text out of the IDE's error window.
LiveCode 9.6.3 IDE. Untested; written from the object path reported at runtime:
field id 1004 of group id 1003 of card id 1002 of stack
".../Toolset/palettes/reverrordisplay.livecodescript"
The IDE shows execution errors in stack "revErrorDisplay". Its fields are
locked, so the text cannot be selected by hand; a script can still read it.

scripts.title: LIB_MCP standalone launcher (xt3d_MCP.exe, port 8767)
scripts.description: Tiny stack script for the LIB_MCP compile-check standalone: finds lib_mcp.livecodescript above its .exe and starts the server. The pattern for standalones that load their real code from files.
header: Stack script for LIB_MCP/standalone/xt3d_MCP.livecode, the standalone LIB_MCP server.
Paste it as the stack script, save, and build a standalone (Windows is enough).
At start it walks up from its own .exe until it finds livecode/lib_mcp.livecodescript
(the build lands in standalone/<StackName>/Windows x86-64/, so that is LIB_MCP's own
folder), loads the server from there and starts it on port 8767. Changes to the server
file therefore need no rebuild; only changes to this script do.
